title: You thought the attack meant God abandoned you.
paragraphs: You thought the attack meant God abandoned you.
That’s the lie.
The pressure increased because something is about to break open.
The enemy rarely wastes energy on people who are already asleep. But when Heaven is preparing a resurrection, a breakthrough, a calling, a restoration, or a transformation… hell starts moving early.
That’s why some of the darkest moments in Scripture happened right before God revealed His power.
Jesus Himself walked into this pattern.

He was betrayed.
Mocked.
Beaten.
Abandoned.
Then buried behind a stone while hell celebrated too early.
But on the third day…
Everything changed.

“And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day.”
— Luke 24:46
Read that again.
The suffering came before the resurrection.
The silence came before the victory.
The burial came before the breakthrough.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Satan studies patterns.
He cannot stop God’s plan, but he tries to pressure people into quitting before they reach the moment God appointed for their deliverance.
That’s why the attack intensifies right before your “third day.”
Not necessarily a literal 72 hours.
The “third day” in Scripture often represents divine turnaround, fulfilled promise, resurrection power, and God stepping into impossible situations.
Abraham saw it.

“On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.”
— Genesis 22:4
That was the mountain where God would test him and reveal Himself as Provider.
Esther saw it.

“Now it came to pass on the third day, that Esther put on her royal apparel…”
— Esther 5:1
That was the day favor interrupted destruction.
Israel saw it.

“And be ready against the third day: for the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people…”
— Exodus 19:11
Hosea prophesied it.

“After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.”
— Hosea 6:2
And Jesus fulfilled it.
The enemy understands that when God is about to move, people become dangerous to darkness.
So the attacks come first.

Confusion.
Temptation.
Isolation.
Fear.
Exhaustion.
Offense.
Delay.
Heavy thoughts you can’t explain.

Suddenly everybody misunderstands you.
Doors close.
Your mind feels assaulted.
Old sins come calling again.
The temptation becomes stronger than it was months ago.
God saw it.
You knew something spiritual was happening.

Because some attacks are not random.
They are resistance against your next season.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
Look carefully through Scripture and you’ll notice something terrifying about Satan’s strategy.
He attacks identity before destiny.
Before Jesus began His ministry, Satan met Him in the wilderness.

“If thou be the Son of God…”
— Matthew 4:3
That attack was aimed at identity.
Because if the enemy can make you question who God says you are, he can delay where God is taking you.
Some of you are under attack not because you are weak…
But because you are close.

Close to repentance.
Close to freedom.
Close to obedience.
Close to finally surrendering fully to Christ.
Close to becoming the version of you hell fears.
That’s why the warfare increased after you started praying seriously.
That’s why temptation exploded after you decided to walk away from sin.
That’s why anxiety intensified after God called you deeper.
The enemy attacks transitions.
Pharaoh increased Israel’s suffering right before deliverance.
Judas betrayed Jesus right before resurrection.
Job lost everything right before restoration.
Peter was sifted right before leadership.
And many believers mistake spiritual resistance as proof God left them, when in reality the resistance is often evidence that the enemy sees what’s coming before they do.
But here is the danger…
Not every attack means breakthrough.

Sometimes suffering comes because of disobedience.
Sometimes consequences are self-inflicted.
Sometimes people call spiritual warfare what is actually rebellion, pride, compromise, or unrepented sin.
Scripture must stay balanced.
You cannot claim a “third day miracle” while refusing repentance.
Jesus did not die so people could continue living comfortably in sin.
The Gospel is not motivational therapy.
It is a death sentence to the old self.

“Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out…”
— Acts 3:19
That’s the part many avoid.
Because everybody wants resurrection power…
But few want crucifixion.
Few want surrender.
Few want holiness.
Few want to forgive the people who wounded them.
Few want to kill the secret sin they protect in darkness.
But your third day begins the moment you stop running from Christ and fully surrender to Him.

Not halfway.
Not emotionally.
Not publicly while privately resisting Him.
Fully.
Because Satan’s greatest fear is not your talent.
It’s your obedience to Jesus.
A surrendered believer filled with the Holy Spirit becomes dangerous to darkness.
That’s why the enemy tries to wear people down before they reach the place of transformation.

He whispers:
“Give up.”
“Go back.”
“Compromise.”
“God isn’t listening.”
“You’ll never change.”
But the cross already exposed him as defeated.

“And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.”
— Colossians 2:15
The resurrection was not symbolic poetry.
It was the declaration that sin, death, hell, and Satan do not get the final word.
Jesus does.
And maybe that’s why your battle became so intense recently.
Because the enemy wants you buried emotionally before God raises you spiritually.

He wants you offended before reconciliation.
Distracted before purpose.
Addicted before freedom.
Numb before awakening.
He wants you to quit on day two.
Because day three terrifies hell.
The empty tomb still shakes darkness.
And if you belong to Christ, your story is no longer defined by what tried to kill you.
It’s defined by the One who walked out of the grave.

“Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life…”
— John 11:25
Not “I can resurrect.”
“I AM the resurrection.”
That changes everything.

So if you’ve been under pressure lately…
If your mind has been exhausted…
If temptation has increased…
If you’ve been fighting thoughts you never expected…
Do not automatically assume God abandoned you.

Examine yourself.
Repent where needed.
Return fully to Christ.
Stay rooted in Scripture.
Pray even when you feel nothing.
Obey even when emotions scream otherwise.
Because sometimes the darkest night comes right before God changes everything.
Because some people are entertaining darkness while others are preparing for resurrection.
Choose carefully.
